thread.title: FANG Stocks Early Winners In First-Quarter Earnings Season

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: FANG Stocks Early Winners In First-Quarter Earnings Season
text:
The first-quarter earnings season has been a good one for leading tech stocks involved in hot online businesses such as cloud computing services, internet advertising and subscription video on demand. The FANG stocks have shown particular strength, though, thanks to those businesses.
X Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOGL ) all cheered the market with their March-quarter reports.
They stand in contrast to other facets of tech, such as the chip sector. That group has been struggling this earning season, especially those companies exposed to the maturing smartphone market.
Suppliers to Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone have been hard hit as news reports point to cuts in production orders. Investors also are worried that the semiconductor sector could be entering a down cycle. Pockets of strength include memory chips and graphics processors.

Facebook Sales Growth Impresses Facebook shook off recent data privacy concerns with its first-quarter results late Wednesday, which blew past expectations . Facebook's revenue rose 49% year over year to $11.97 billion, topping the 47% growth seen in the previous two quarters and showing the strength of its advertising-based social networking service. Earnings per share rose 63% to $1.69.
"We think that ads is a great business model that is aligned with our mission," Facebook Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said on a conference call with analysts. "We want to build a service that can help connect everyone around the world so we want to offer that service for free."
Facebook ended the quarter with 1.45 billion daily active users, up 13% from a year ago and matching views. It had 2.2 billion monthly active users, also up 13% and meeting estimates.
Next up for Facebook is the company's annual developer conference, F8, in San Jose, Calif. The two-day conference starts Tuesday.
Amazon Trounces Wall Street Views E-commerce giant Amazon saw its stock spike to an all-time high after it posted better-than-expected first-quarter results late Thursday.
Amazon's revenue rose 43% year over year to $51 billion, ahead of the consensus estimate of $49.9 billion. Its adjusted earnings per share surged 121% to $3.27, obliterating analyst predictions for $1.26. It also guided to sales above views for the current quarter.
In addition to online shopping, Amazon plays in such fast-growing markets as cloud computing infrastructure services and subscription video on demand.
On April 18, Amazon Chief Executive Jeff Bezos revealed in a letter to shareholders that the company has over 100 million paid Prime members globally. Prime offers free shipping, access to Amazon's streaming video and music services, and other benefits.
Amazon announced Thursday that it plans to raise the annual cost of Prime membership by 20% to $119, from $99, flexing its pricing power.
"The Prime program continues to drive great strength in our top line," Amazon Chief Financial Officer Brian Olsavsky said on a conference call with analysts. But costs have been rising as Amazon expands free shipping options and adds more benefits like Prime Video, he said.
Netflix Subscriber Gains Wow Internet television network Netflix helped kick off the earnings season on April 16, when it crushed Wall Street's targets for subscriber growth.
Netflix added 7.41 million new streaming subscribers in the first quarter , beating its target for 6.35 million. It ended the March quarter with 125 million subscribers worldwide, including 56.71 million in the U.S. and 68.29 million in international markets.
For the second quarter, Netflix expects to add 6.2 million subscribers worldwide, topping Wall Street's target of 5.2 million net new subscribers in the period.
Netflix credited its subscriber gains to its aggressive push to add exclusive, original content. Popular shows on Netflix include "Stranger Things," "Lost in Space," "Money Heist" and "13 Reasons Why."
"We've got some great momentum, and we're very excited about that, but we have a long way to go in terms of earning all of the viewing that we want to," Netflix CEO Reed Hastings said in a conference call with analysts.
Alphabet Stock Consolidates Alphabet, parent of search giant Google, posted first-quarter results that topped expectations on April 23. It earned $9.93 a share, up 28% year over year, on sales of $31.15 billion, up 26%, in the March quarter. Analysts expected $9.31 and $30.31 billion.
Alphabet stock fell on the quarterly report, due to a reported spike in spending, but it has held up relatively well. It has been consolidating for the past 13 weeks, establishing a buy point of 1,198.10.
Alphabet has been diversifying beyond its core search advertising business into video content, cloud computing, consumer electronics and self-driving cars.
